title: Reporting & CARO 2020 (SA 700/705 Report Wording, Sec 143 Duties, Fraud Reporting)
description: CA Final – Auditing and Assurance | Advanced MCQ practice bank on the Reporting chapter: classification of the financial reporting framework (fair presentation vs compliance); framing of the audit report under SA 700 and SA 705 (opinion, basis for opinion, emphasis of matter, other matter and material uncertainty related to going concern paragraphs); auditor duties under section 143(1), 143(3), 143(11) and 143(12) of the Companies Act, 2013 including fraud reporting in Form ADT-4; and reporting under CARO, 2020 – applicability and exemptions and clauses (i) to (xxi). Case-study heavy, application-oriented, strictly confined to the source material.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the classification of a financial reporting framework (FRF) for the purpose of reporting:
1. A fair presentation framework requires compliance with the requirements of the FRF and further acknowledges that, to achieve fair presentation of the FS, management may provide disclosures beyond those specifically required by the FRF.
2. A compliance framework requires compliance with the requirements of the FRF and, in addition, expressly contemplates disclosures beyond those specifically required.
3. At the reporting phase, a fair presentation framework is reported on by stating that the FS give a true and fair view of / present fairly as per the applicable FRF.
4. At the reporting phase, a compliance framework is reported on by stating that the FS have been prepared, in all material respects, as per the applicable FRF.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is the only incorrect one: the acknowledgment that management may provide disclosures beyond those specifically required is the very feature that separates a fair presentation framework from a compliance framework, and a compliance framework requires nothing more than compliance with the requirements of the FRF. Statements 1, 3 and 4 reproduce the two rows of the classification table - requirement/meaning and reporting phase. The decisive marker to look for in any framework description is the phrase 'beyond those specifically required by FRF'; where it is absent the framework is a compliance framework, and the reporting-phase wording then changes from true and fair view / present fairly to preparation in all material respects.

questions.category: Financial Reporting Framework - Compliance Framework Reporting
questions.question:
Case: Kaveri Agro Products (India) Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of a foreign group, prepares its statutory FS for FY 2024-25 under a financial reporting framework prescribed by that country's regulator. The framework lays down an exhaustive set of recognition, measurement, presentation and disclosure requirements, requires compliance with those requirements, and contains no acknowledgment whatever that management may make additional disclosures in order to achieve fair presentation. The auditor identifies no departures from the framework during the audit.

Which of the following is the most appropriate reporting-phase conclusion for the auditor's report on these FS?
options: The FS give a true and fair view of the state of affairs of the entity as at March 31, 2025.
The FS present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the entity, and are equally capable of being reported as giving a true and fair view because no departures were detected.
The FS have been prepared, in all material respects, as per the applicable financial reporting framework.
The FS give a true and fair view in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in India, since the absence of departures is common to both frameworks.
questions.explanation: The framework described is a compliance framework: it requires compliance with its requirements and does not acknowledge that management may provide disclosures beyond those specifically required. The reporting-phase wording attaching to such a framework is that the FS have been prepared, in all material respects, as per the applicable FRF. A conclusion in terms of a true and fair view of the state of affairs belongs to the fair presentation row of the table and is therefore unavailable here, and so is one which adds the words 'in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in India' - a reference to a framework that is not the one applied. A conclusion which blends the two forms is equally wrong, because the source treats them as two mutually exclusive reporting-phase conclusions; and the fact that no departures were found does not convert a compliance framework into a fair presentation framework, since the classification depends on the framework itself and not on the result of the audit.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements drawn from the extracts of the Opinion Paragraph of an audit report framed under a fair presentation framework:
1. The clause 'except for the effects of matter described in Basis for Qualified Opinion section of our report' appears in the qualified opinion extract, while 'because of omission of information / significance of matter mentioned in Basis for Adverse Opinion section of our report' appears in the adverse opinion extract.
2. The preamble 'In our opinion and to the best of our information and according to explanations given to us' is common to the unmodified, qualified and adverse opinion extracts, and is also retained in the disclaimer of opinion extract.
3. The unmodified and qualified extracts speak of the state of affairs of the entity as at March 31, 20XX, whereas the adverse opinion extract speaks of the financial position of the entity as at that date.
4. The disclaimer of opinion extract states that the auditor has not been able to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to provide a basis for an audit opinion, and that he does not express an opinion.
Which of the above statements are NOT correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 only
2 and 4 only
3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statement 2 alone is incorrect. The disclaimer extract as framed does not carry the opinion-giving preamble; it opens with the engagement statement ('We have engaged to audit the FS of XYZ Ltd'), proceeds to 'We do not express an opinion on FS of entity', and rests that on inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence - the auditor has no basis on which an opinion could be given, so a preamble asserting opinion would be contradictory. Statements 1, 3 and 4 are faithful to the extracts: 'except for' distinguishes the qualified construction from the 'because of' construction of the adverse and disclaimer extracts, the adverse extract alone substitutes 'financial position' for 'state of affairs', and the disclaimer is the extract founded on evidence that could not be obtained. The decisive point being tested is that loss of the preamble is peculiar to the disclaimer and does not follow from modification as such.

questions.category: SA 705 - Modification Types and Distinctive Phrases
questions.question:
Match Column I with Column II.
Column I (Type of opinion / modification)
P. Unmodified opinion
Q. Qualified opinion
R. Adverse opinion
S. Disclaimer of opinion
Column II (Distinctive phrase in the Opinion Paragraph extract)
1. '... we have not been able to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to provide a basis for audit opinion on these FS.'
2. '... FS give a true and fair view in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in India, of state of affairs of entity as at March 31, 20XX, and profit/loss and its cash flows for the year ended on that date', with no qualifying clause interposed.
3. '... except for the effects of matter described in Basis for Qualified Opinion section of our report, FS give a true and fair view ...'
4. '... because of omission of information / significance of matter mentioned in Basis for Adverse Opinion section of our report, FS do not give a true and fair view ... of financial position of entity as at March 31, 20XX ...'
Which pairing is correct?
questions.explanation: Each modification is identifiable by one characteristic clause. The unmodified extract makes the true and fair view assertion on the state of affairs with nothing interposed; the qualified extract interposes 'except for the effects of matter described in Basis for Qualified Opinion section of our report' and still asserts a true and fair view; the adverse extract substitutes 'because of', denies a true and fair view and refers to the financial position of the entity; and only the disclaimer extract rests on inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence and expressly refuses to express an opinion. A pairing that swaps the 'except for' and 'because of' clauses of Q and R is the commonest error, because both are modifications; equally, a pairing that attaches the disclaimer phrase to the adverse opinion overlooks that an adverse opinion is a positive conclusion that the FS are misleading, whereas a disclaimer is the absence of any conclusion because no basis for one exists.

questions.question:
Case: Vidarbha Steel Ltd, an unlisted public company, prepares its financial statements in accordance with Ind AS, a financial reporting framework which requires compliance with its requirements and acknowledges that to achieve fair presentation of the FS management may provide disclosures beyond those specifically required. In the audit of FY 2024-25 the auditor, CA Rane & Associates, found that the company had neither recognised a liability of ₹148 crore for environmental remediation ordered by the National Green Tribunal nor disclosed the matter in the notes to the FS. Management agreed that no provision had been made and that no note had been written, and the auditor concluded that this was a departure from the requirements of the applicable financial reporting framework. The matter was material, but its effect was confined to the said liability, the omitted disclosure, the consequential tax effect and the resulting overstatement of profit; the remaining elements of the FS were, in the auditor's judgment, still capable of being read as giving a true and fair view but for that matter. There was no limitation on the scope of the audit and the auditor had obtained complete evidence about the NGT order and the amount involved.

Which modification, if any, of the opinion is the most appropriate in these circumstances?
options: Adverse opinion, because any departure from a fair presentation framework prevents the FS from giving a true and fair view.
Qualified opinion, because the FS give a true and fair view except for the effects of the described matter.
Disclaimer of opinion, because ₹148 crore is a large amount.
Emphasis of Matter paragraph referring to the NGT liability, because the matter is important and needs to be highlighted for users.
questions.explanation: The auditor holds complete evidence and has identified a departure from the requirements of the framework, so the problem is a misstatement and not an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence - which takes the disclaimer out of court, since that extract is available only where evidence could not be obtained. The effect of the misstatement is confined to identified items and the balance of the FS can still be read as giving a true and fair view but for the matter, which is exactly what the qualified extract says in the words 'except for the effects of matter described in Basis for Qualified Opinion section of our report'. An adverse extract would assert that the FS do not give a true and fair view, a conclusion the auditor's own finding excludes. The Emphasis of Matter paragraph is unavailable because it is drawn up for a matter already presented or disclosed in the FS and closes with 'Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter' - the opposite of the position here, where neither a provision nor a note exists.

questions.category: SA 705 - Basis for Qualified Opinion Section
questions.question:
Case: Vidarbha Steel Ltd, an unlisted public company, prepares its financial statements in accordance with Ind AS, a financial reporting framework which requires compliance with its requirements and acknowledges that to achieve fair presentation of the FS management may provide disclosures beyond those specifically required. In the audit of FY 2024-25 the auditor, CA Rane & Associates, found that the company had neither recognised a liability of ₹148 crore for environmental remediation ordered by the National Green Tribunal nor disclosed the matter in the notes to the FS. Management agreed that no provision had been made and that no note had been written, and the auditor concluded that this was a departure from the requirements of the applicable financial reporting framework. The matter was material, but its effect was confined to the said liability, the omitted disclosure, the consequential tax effect and the resulting overstatement of profit; the remaining elements of the FS were, in the auditor's judgment, still capable of being read as giving a true and fair view but for that matter. There was no limitation on the scope of the audit and the auditor had obtained complete evidence about the NGT order and the amount involved.

Which of the following actions should the auditor take in framing the report?
1. Amend the heading 'Basis for Opinion' to 'Basis for Qualified Opinion'.
2. Include within that section the description of the matter giving rise to the modification, namely the unrecognised NGT liability and the omitted disclosure.
3. Retain the heading 'Basis for Opinion' unchanged, since a qualification is only a mild form of modification.
4. Refer, in the Opinion Paragraph, to the section of the report in which the matter giving rise to the modification is described.
options: 1 and 2 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Whenever the auditor modifies the opinion on the FS - by qualification, adverse opinion or disclaimer - the auditor shall amend the heading 'Basis for Opinion' to correspond to the modification, here 'Basis for Qualified Opinion', and shall include within that section the description of the matter giving rise to the modification. Both limbs are mandatory and the requirement is not scaled down according to how mild the auditor considers the qualification to be, so action 3 fails. Action 4 does not arise from an independent rule but from the prescribed wording itself: the qualified opinion extract is drafted with the cross-reference 'except for the effects of matter described in Basis for Qualified Opinion section of our report', so the Opinion Paragraph of its own terms points the reader to that section.

questions.question:
Case: Vidarbha Steel Ltd, an unlisted public company, prepares its financial statements in accordance with Ind AS, a financial reporting framework which requires compliance with its requirements and acknowledges that to achieve fair presentation of the FS management may provide disclosures beyond those specifically required. In the audit of FY 2024-25 the auditor, CA Rane & Associates, found that the company had neither recognised a liability of ₹148 crore for environmental remediation ordered by the National Green Tribunal nor disclosed the matter in the notes to the FS. Management agreed that no provision had been made and that no note had been written, and the auditor concluded that this was a departure from the requirements of the applicable financial reporting framework. The matter was material, but its effect was confined to the said liability, the omitted disclosure, the consequential tax effect and the resulting overstatement of profit; the remaining elements of the FS were, in the auditor's judgment, still capable of being read as giving a true and fair view but for that matter. There was no limitation on the scope of the audit and the auditor had obtained complete evidence about the NGT order and the amount involved.

Which of the following is the most appropriate content of the Opinion Paragraph for this report?
options: 'In our opinion and to the best of our information and according to explanations given to us, because of omission of information / significance of the matter mentioned in Basis for Adverse Opinion section of our report, the FS do not give a true and fair view in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in India of the financial position of the entity as at March 31, 2025, and of its profit/loss and its cash flows for the year ended on that date.'

'In our opinion and to the best of our information and according to explanations given to us, the FS give a true and fair view ... of the state of affairs of the entity as at March 31, 2025 ... We draw attention to the Note describing the NGT liability. Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.'

'In our opinion and to the best of our information and according to explanations given to us, except for the effects of matter described in Basis for Qualified Opinion section of our report, the FS give a true and fair view in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in India, of the state of affairs of the entity as at March 31, 2025, and of its profit/loss and its cash flows for the year ended on that date.'

'We have engaged to audit the FS of Vidarbha Steel Ltd. We do not express an opinion on the FS of the entity. Because of significance of the matter described in the Basis for Disclaimer of Opinion section of our report, we have not been able to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to provide a basis for an audit opinion on these FS.'
questions.explanation: The conclusion reached is a qualification, so the Opinion Paragraph must be the qualified extract: it preserves the preamble 'In our opinion and to the best of our information and according to explanations given to us', interposes 'except for the effects of matter described in Basis for Qualified Opinion section of our report', and continues to assert a true and fair view of the state of affairs of the entity as at the balance sheet date and of its profit/loss and cash flows. The adverse extract is unsuitable because its 'because of' construction denies a true and fair view of the FS as a whole, which the auditor's own finding on confinement does not support, and it also substitutes 'financial position' for 'state of affairs'. Giving an unmodified opinion and then adding an Emphasis of Matter sentence stating that the opinion is not modified would flatly contradict the qualification, and cannot be used for a liability that has been neither recognised nor disclosed. The disclaimer extract is available only where sufficient appropriate audit evidence could not be obtained, which the case expressly rules out.

questions.question:
Case: Vidarbha Steel Ltd, an unlisted public company, prepares its financial statements in accordance with Ind AS, a financial reporting framework which requires compliance with its requirements and acknowledges that to achieve fair presentation of the FS management may provide disclosures beyond those specifically required. In the audit of FY 2024-25 the auditor, CA Rane & Associates, found that the company had neither recognised a liability of ₹148 crore for environmental remediation ordered by the National Green Tribunal nor disclosed the matter in the notes to the FS. Management agreed that no provision had been made and that no note had been written, and the auditor concluded that this was a departure from the requirements of the applicable financial reporting framework. The matter was material, but its effect was confined to the said liability, the omitted disclosure, the consequential tax effect and the resulting overstatement of profit; the remaining elements of the FS were, in the auditor's judgment, still capable of being read as giving a true and fair view but for that matter. There was no limitation on the scope of the audit and the auditor had obtained complete evidence about the NGT order and the amount involved.

Now assume that the unrecognised and undisclosed liability is ₹2,150 crore against net worth of ₹940 crore and revenue of ₹1,180 crore, that its effect runs through the balance sheet, the statement of profit and loss, the cash flow statement and every ratio users rely upon, and that the auditor concludes that the FS taken as a whole cannot be said to give a true and fair view. There is still no limitation on the scope of the audit. What changes in the report, and how?
options: The opinion becomes a disclaimer, because the amount is too large for any opinion to be given.
Nothing changes in the Opinion Paragraph; only the description in the basis section is enlarged.
The opinion becomes adverse, but the preamble 'In our opinion and to the best of our information and according to explanations given to us' must now be dropped.

The opinion becomes adverse, and the basis section heading changes to 'Basis for Adverse Opinion'; the extract asserts that because of omission of information / significance of the matter the FS do not give a true and fair view.
questions.explanation: One fact moves - the significance of the effect. The departure now pervades the FS so that they as a whole do not give a true and fair view, which is precisely what the adverse extract states in the words 'because of omission of information / significance of matter mentioned in Basis for Adverse Opinion section of our report, FS do not give a true and fair view', and the heading of the basis section is amended to match. A disclaimer is unavailable because the modification still arises from a known departure on which the auditor has complete evidence, and the disclaimer extract speaks only of not being able to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence. A mere 'except for the effects of' qualification would misstate the auditor's revised conclusion. The suggestion that the preamble must now be dropped is also wrong, because the adverse extract, unlike the disclaimer extract, retains the preamble; what does change in it is 'state of affairs' giving way to 'financial position'.

questions.question:
Case: Ooty Valley Tea Estates Ltd is being audited for FY 2024-25. Its biological asset - 1,240 hectares of tea bushes across three geographically separated estates - is carried at ₹486 crore, and trade receivables of ₹210 crore relate to 46 export debtors in five countries. The auditor was denied access to all three estates for the purpose of physical verification owing to a prolonged workers' stir, and receivable confirmations were either not returned or returned with contradictions. No alternative procedure available to him could produce reliable evidence about the existence and valuation of the biological asset or the recoverability of the receivables, and together these two items form a substantial majority of the assets shown in the balance sheet. Management has recorded both items on the basis of its own internal estimates and has described that position in the notes.

Based on the above case, which of the following statements are correct?
1. The auditor should disclaim an opinion because he has not been able to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to provide a basis for an audit opinion.
2. The auditor should give an adverse opinion, because the carrying values of the biological asset and the receivables may be misstated.
3. The Opinion Paragraph should state that the auditor does not express an opinion on the FS of the entity and should not carry the words 'In our opinion and to the best of our information and according to explanations given to us'.
4. The heading 'Basis for Opinion' should be amended to 'Basis for Disclaimer of Opinion' and the description of the matters giving rise to the disclaimer should be included in that section.
options: 1, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The decisive characteristic is the nature of the problem, not its size. The auditor cannot obtain evidence, so the appropriate modification is a disclaimer; an adverse opinion is unavailable because it is a positive assertion that the FS do not give a true and fair view, and an auditor who has no basis for any opinion cannot assert the opposite of a true and fair view either - the possible misstatement is unquantified precisely because evidence is missing. The disclaimer extract states that the auditor does not express an opinion, grounds it on inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence, and alone among the four extracts omits the opinion-giving preamble. Statement 4 applies the general requirement that whenever the opinion is modified - qualification, adverse opinion or disclaimer alike - the heading is amended to name the modification and the description of the matter giving rise to it is placed within that section.

questions.question:
Case: Ooty Valley Tea Estates Ltd is being audited for FY 2024-25. Its biological asset - 1,240 hectares of tea bushes across three geographically separated estates - is carried at ₹486 crore, and trade receivables of ₹210 crore relate to 46 export debtors in five countries. The auditor was denied access to all three estates for the purpose of physical verification owing to a prolonged workers' stir, and receivable confirmations were either not returned or returned with contradictions. No alternative procedure available to him could produce reliable evidence about the existence and valuation of the biological asset or the recoverability of the receivables, and together these two items form a substantial majority of the assets shown in the balance sheet. Management has recorded both items on the basis of its own internal estimates and has described that position in the notes.

Assume instead that the workers' stir is resolved before the report is signed, the auditor verifies the estates and obtains satisfactory evidence on the receivables, and in doing so establishes that the company has depreciated the entire ₹486 crore biological asset in a single year contrary to Ind AS. The resulting error of ₹92 crore is material but confined to that asset, the resulting profit figure and the consequential tax effect, leaving the balance of the FS reliable.

How does the report change?
options: Nothing changes; the auditor must still disclaim, because access was initially refused for the planned procedures.
The auditor should give an adverse opinion, since any departure from a fair presentation framework is a departure from the framework as a whole.
The auditor should give a qualified opinion, because the FS give a true and fair view except for the effects of the matter described in the Basis for Qualified Opinion section.
The auditor should give an unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph, because the error has been located and quantified with precision.
questions.explanation: Two decisive facts move. The inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence disappears once the alternative and subsequent procedures produce satisfactory evidence, so the disclaimer loses the only foundation it ever had - an initial refusal of access is not itself the subject of the opinion paragraph once the evidence is secured. What remains is a known, quantified departure from the requirements of the framework, so the choice lies between qualification and an adverse opinion, and the adverse extract requires the FS taken as a whole to be incapable of giving a true and fair view, which is not so where the effect is confined to one asset and the consequential profit and tax figures. Precision in quantifying an error is a reason for modifying the opinion rather than a reason for leaving it unmodified and merely emphasising the matter, since the Emphasis of Matter paragraph presupposes a matter appropriately presented or disclosed in the FS and closes by stating that the opinion is not modified.

questions.question:
Case: Brahmaputra Infra Ltd has during FY 2024-25 become a party to an arbitration claim by a highway authority seeking ₹260 crore. After taking legal advice the company has recognised no provision and has set out fully in Note 38 of the FS the nature of the claim, the amount claimed, management's and its counsel's assessment of the outcome and the fact that the outcome cannot be predicted with certainty. The auditor is satisfied that both the accounting and the disclosure comply with the applicable financial reporting framework, and judges the matter to be of such importance that it is fundamental to users' understanding of the FS. He intends to draw users' attention to it without changing his opinion.

Which of the following actions should the auditor take?
1. Include an Emphasis of Matter paragraph in the form 'We draw attention to Note 38 of FS. Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.'
2. Amend the heading 'Basis for Opinion' to reflect the addition of the Emphasis of Matter paragraph.
3. Refer in the paragraph to the specific Note of the FS in which the matter is presented or disclosed.
4. Modify the opinion, because a matter that is fundamental to users' understanding cannot coexist with an unmodified opinion.
options: 1, 3 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
questions.explanation: The Emphasis of Matter paragraph as framed has exactly two sentences - a draw of attention to a specified Note of the FS and the statement 'Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter' - so actions 1 and 3 together give it correctly, and the reference to Note 38 is essential because the paragraph is available only where the matter is already presented or disclosed in the FS. Action 2 is wrong: the obligation to amend the heading arises only when the auditor modifies the opinion by qualification, adverse opinion or disclaimer, and an Emphasis of Matter paragraph is expressly not a modification. Action 4 inverts the logic of the paragraph; the closing sentence is what allows the auditor to highlight a fundamental matter without qualifying, and the auditor's finding that the accounting and disclosure comply with the framework is the fact that keeps the opinion unmodified.

questions.category: SA 700 - Emphasis of Matter - Assertion Reason
questions.question:
Assertion (A): An Emphasis of Matter paragraph included in an audit report does not constitute a modification of the auditor's opinion.
Reason (R): The prescribed Emphasis of Matter paragraph closes with the sentence 'Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter', and its opening sentence draws attention to a Note of the financial statements, that is, to a matter already presented or disclosed therein.
In the context of the above, which of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation: The Emphasis of Matter paragraph as framed consists of two sentences only - 'We draw attention to Note X of FS.' and 'Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.' The second is itself the operative statement that the opinion stands unmodified, and that is why the paragraph does not attract the consequences attached to a modification, namely amending the 'Basis for Opinion' heading and describing within that section the matter giving rise to the modification. The first sentence supplies the further reason the paragraph is available at all: because the matter is already presented or disclosed in the FS, there is no departure or omission to report. R therefore explains A both textually and logically. Contrast the Other Matter paragraph, whose prescribed content is a statement of the relevant matter followed by the same closing sentence and which likewise does not modify the opinion.

questions.category: SA 700 - Emphasis of Matter and Other Matter
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Emphasis of Matter and Other Matter paragraphs of an audit report:
1. Both the Emphasis of Matter paragraph and the Other Matter paragraph close with the sentence 'Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.'
2. The Emphasis of Matter paragraph opens by drawing attention to a specified Note of the FS, whereas the Other Matter paragraph is framed simply as a statement of the relevant matter followed by the non-modification sentence.
3. Inclusion of either paragraph obliges the auditor to amend the heading 'Basis for Opinion' so as to describe that paragraph.
4. Neither paragraph is a form of modified opinion; the modifications are qualification, adverse opinion and disclaimer of opinion.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 compare the two prescriptions exactly as framed: the Emphasis of Matter paragraph reads 'We draw attention to Note X of FS. Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.' while the Other Matter paragraph reads 'Relevant Matter. Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.' Statement 4 follows from the requirement governing the basis section, which is attracted only when the auditor modifies the opinion by qualification, adverse opinion or disclaimer. Statement 3 is therefore wrong, and it is the natural confusion to test: because these paragraphs and the modified opinions all sit in the same region of the report, candidates often treat the addition of any paragraph as a modification, whereas the closing sentence of these two paragraphs says in terms that the opinion is not modified.

questions.category: SA 570 / SA 700 - Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern
questions.question:
Case: Konark Spinners Ltd, an unlisted public company, prepares its FS under Ind AS. Its lead bank has recalled working-capital limits of ₹430 crore, payable within 60 days. Note 42 of the FS for FY 2024-25 sets out the recall, describes management's proposed one-time settlement with the consortium, and states that a material uncertainty exists which may cast significant doubt on the company's ability to continue as a going concern; the FS are drawn up on the going concern basis, and the auditor is satisfied that use of that basis remains appropriate, that the accounting is correct and that the disclosure is complete. Separately, an export subsidiary was sold during the year and the comparative figures include its results; the auditor wishes to refer in his report to the scope of his responsibilities in respect of those comparatives, there being no matter presented or disclosed in the FS in that regard.

Based on the above case, which paragraph should the auditor use for the going concern matter and what should it contain?
options: An Emphasis of Matter paragraph reading 'We draw attention to Note 42 of FS. Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.', this being sufficient because the matter is already disclosed in a Note and nothing further need be said about it.

An Other Matter paragraph reading 'Recall of working capital limits. Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.', since the recall is a matter relevant to the audit and to users' understanding of the report.
A qualified opinion, because significant doubt about the company's ability to continue as a going concern can be brought to the notice of users only by modifying the opinion on the FS.

A paragraph headed Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern which draws attention to Note 42, states that as set out in that Note the event or condition indicates that a material uncertainty exists that may cast significant doubt on the company's ability to continue as a going concern, and states that the opinion is not modified in respect of the matter.
questions.explanation: The source prescribes a separate Going Concern paragraph, styled Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern, whose content is longer than that of the ordinary Emphasis of Matter paragraph: it draws attention to the Note, repeats what the Note states - that the event or condition indicates that a material uncertainty exists that may cast significant doubt on the company's ability to continue as a going concern - and closes with the non-modification sentence. A plain Emphasis of Matter paragraph would omit the substantive going concern statement required here, and the Other Matter paragraph is framed without any reference to a Note and so cannot carry a matter that is disclosed in one. Modification is not required because the uncertainty is fully disclosed and the going concern basis has been accepted as appropriate; the prescribed paragraph is itself drafted on the footing that the opinion is not modified.

questions.category: SA 570 / SA 705 - Going Concern Disclosure Omitted
questions.question:
Case: Konark Spinners Ltd, an unlisted public company, prepares its FS under Ind AS. Its lead bank has recalled working-capital limits of ₹430 crore, payable within 60 days. The FS for FY 2024-25 are drawn up on the going concern basis and the auditor is satisfied that use of that basis remains appropriate.

Assume that the FS contain no note about the recall, no statement of any material uncertainty and no description of management's proposed resolution; management's position is that disclosing the recall would prejudice the settlement discussions. The auditor regards the matter as material.

Given this assumption, can the auditor use the Going Concern Paragraph headed Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern, and if not, why?
options: Yes, because a material uncertainty relating to the going concern of the entity is always brought out through that paragraph, and the opinion remains unmodified whatever the state of the disclosure.
Yes, but it must be given the form of an Emphasis of Matter paragraph, since there is no Note of the FS to which the auditor could draw the attention of users.

No, because the prescribed paragraph draws attention to a Note of the FS and states that the material uncertainty is one as stated in that Note; with no such disclosure that statement cannot be made, and the omission is itself a departure from the framework which calls for modification of the opinion.
No, because that paragraph is available only where the auditor has been unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about management's plans for the coming year.
questions.explanation: The prescribed paragraph is drafted on the assumption that the uncertainty has been disclosed: 'We draw attention to Note X of FS. As stated in Note X, this event or condition indicate that material uncertainty exists that may cast significant doubt on company's ability to continue as going concern.' With no such note the auditor cannot make either the reference or the substantive statement, and what is left before him is an omission of information required by the financial reporting framework - a departure which the report must reflect by modifying the opinion, and the adverse extract expressly contemplates a case arising 'because of omission of information'. The view that the paragraph is available whatever the state of the disclosure and that the opinion remains unmodified overlooks the precondition of an existing disclosure. The proposal to substitute an Emphasis of Matter paragraph, since there is no Note of the FS, replaces the going-concern paragraph with a different one which, being likewise built on a reference to a Note, cannot cure an omission. And the reading that the paragraph is available only where the auditor has been unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about management's plans for the coming year confuses the going concern paragraph, which states that the opinion is not modified, with the disclaimer extract, which is the paragraph founded on inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence.

questions.category: SA 700 - Report Structure and Basis Section Heading
questions.question:
Case: Konark Spinners Ltd, an unlisted public company, prepares its FS under Ind AS. Its lead bank has recalled working-capital limits of ₹430 crore, payable within 60 days. Note 42 of the FS for FY 2024-25 sets out the recall, describes management's proposed one-time settlement with the consortium, and states that a material uncertainty exists which may cast significant doubt on the company's ability to continue as a going concern; the FS are drawn up on the going concern basis, and the auditor is satisfied that use of that basis remains appropriate, that the accounting is correct and that the disclosure is complete. Separately, an export subsidiary was sold during the year and the comparative figures include its results; the auditor wishes to refer in his report to the scope of his responsibilities in respect of those comparatives, there being no matter presented or disclosed in the FS in that regard.

Based on the above case, which of the following statements are correct?
1. The going concern matter is reported in a paragraph which states that the opinion is not modified in respect of it.
2. The matter concerning the comparatives of the sold export subsidiary is reported in an Other Matter paragraph.
3. Because two additional paragraphs appear, the heading 'Basis for Opinion' must be amended to describe them.
4. If the auditor were also to qualify his opinion on some third matter, the description of the matter giving rise to that qualification would have to be placed within the amended basis section.
options: 1, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 read directly off the prescriptions. The material uncertainty paragraph ends with 'Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter', and a matter which is not presented or disclosed in the FS and which concerns the scope of the auditor's responsibilities takes the Other Matter form 'Relevant Matter. Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter' - the case's express statement that nothing is disclosed in the FS on the comparatives is the decisive fact. Statement 3 is wrong because the duty to amend the heading arises only on a modification of the opinion by qualification, adverse opinion or disclaimer; neither a material uncertainty paragraph nor an Other Matter paragraph triggers it, so the heading stays 'Basis for Opinion'. Statement 4 applies the same requirement to a hypothetical qualification, where the heading would become 'Basis for Qualified Opinion' and the description of the matter giving rise to the modification would go inside that section.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Basis for Opinion paragraph of an audit report:
1. The heading 'Basis for Opinion' must be amended to 'Basis for Qualified Opinion', 'Basis for Adverse Opinion' or 'Basis for Disclaimer of Opinion' whenever the auditor modifies his opinion on the FS.
2. The description of the matter giving rise to the modification must be included within the Basis for Opinion section.
3. The requirement to amend the heading is attracted when an Emphasis of Matter paragraph or a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern paragraph is included in the report.
4. Where the modification arises from an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence, only one of the two obligations - amending the heading or describing the matter - needs to be performed.
Which of the above statements are NOT correct?
options: 3 only
3 and 4 only
1 and 2 only
2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statement 3 is incorrect: the source attracts both obligations only when the auditor modifies the opinion, and it names the modifications as qualification, adverse opinion and disclaimer; an Emphasis of Matter paragraph and a material uncertainty paragraph each carry the express statement that the opinion is not modified and therefore leave the heading untouched. Statement 4 is also incorrect, because the requirement is conjunctive - the auditor shall amend the heading and shall include within that section the description of the matter giving rise to the modification - and no relaxation is made for a modification founded on a scope limitation; indeed in a disclaimer the description of the matters not capable of being evidenced is the substance of the section. Statements 1 and 2 are the two limbs of the requirement exactly as given, so any option that excludes either of them is wrong.

questions.category: Integrated - FRF Classification and Opinion Wording
questions.question:
Case: The same audit firm reports for FY 2024-25 on two entities.
Entity A: an Indian company preparing FS under Ind AS, a framework which requires compliance with its requirements and acknowledges that, to achieve fair presentation of the FS, management may provide disclosures beyond those specifically required. On a particular matter the auditor concludes that the FS give a true and fair view except for the effects of that matter.
Entity B: a foreign component of the same group preparing FS under a framework which requires only compliance with its requirements and contains no acknowledgment of additional disclosures to achieve fair presentation. On an identically sized matter the auditor reaches the same conclusion as for Entity A, namely that the FS can be relied upon but for that one matter.

Which of the following statements are correct?
1. Entity A is reported on under a fair presentation framework and Entity B under a compliance framework.
2. The reporting-phase statement for Entity A is that the FS give a true and fair view of / present fairly as per the applicable FRF, while for Entity B it is that the FS have been prepared, in all material respects, as per the applicable FRF.
3. The four Opinion Paragraph extracts for unmodified, qualified, adverse and disclaimer opinions are framed for a fair presentation framework, so the qualified extract used for Entity A cannot be adopted word for word for Entity B.
4. Because the auditor's conclusion on the matter is identical for the two entities, the same form of modification and therefore the same opinion wording applies to both.
options: 1, 3 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The classification turns on one distinguishing feature - whether the framework acknowledges that management may give disclosures beyond those specifically required - so statement 1 is right, and statement 2 states the reporting-phase consequence in the same row of the table: true and fair view / present fairly for a fair presentation framework, preparation in all material respects as per the applicable FRF for a compliance framework. Statement 3 is right because the source heads the four opinion extracts expressly as extracts under a fair presentation framework; the 'true and fair view' construction embedded in the qualified extract therefore cannot be lifted unchanged into a report on compliance-framework FS. Statement 4 confuses two separate decisions: the form of modification may well be the same, but the wording of the resulting opinion paragraph is framework-dependent, so identical conclusions do not produce identical wordings.

questions.question:
Match Column I with Column II.
Column I (Paragraph of the audit report)
P. Emphasis of Matter paragraph
Q. Other Matter paragraph
R. Going Concern paragraph (Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern)
S. Opinion Paragraph where the auditor has been unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence
Column II (Prescribed content as framed)
1. 'Relevant Matter. Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.'
2. 'We draw attention to Note X of FS. As stated in Note X, this event or condition indicate that material uncertainty exists that may cast significant doubt on company's ability to continue as going concern. Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.'
3. 'We have engaged to audit the FS of XYZ Ltd. We do not express an opinion on FS of entity ...'
4. 'We draw attention to Note X of FS. Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.'
Which pairing is correct?
questions.explanation: The Emphasis of Matter paragraph is the shortest draw-of-attention form, closing with the non-modification sentence. The Other Matter paragraph replaces the reference to a Note with a statement of the relevant matter and keeps the same closing sentence. The Going Concern paragraph is the draw-of-attention form expanded by the substantive statement that, as stated in the Note, the event or condition indicates that a material uncertainty exists that may cast significant doubt on the company's ability to continue as a going concern. The extract beginning with the engagement statement and the refusal to express an opinion belongs to a disclaimer of opinion. The likeliest error is a pairing which swaps Q and R, but a going concern material uncertainty is by definition disclosed in a Note of the FS, so it cannot take a form framed without any reference to a Note, and conversely a matter not disclosed in the FS cannot be introduced by drawing attention to a Note that does not exist.

questions.category: SA 705 / SA 570 - Two Matters in One Report
questions.question:
Case: Meghnaghat Alloys Ltd is audited for FY 2024-25 and the auditor reports two matters.
Matter 1: inventory of ₹74 crore has been valued at sale price below cost for one product line in breach of the applicable financial reporting framework; the amount is material but its effect is confined to that line and to the resulting profit figures.
Matter 2: the company has correctly recognised and fully disclosed in Note 27 a material uncertainty arising from the loss of its only bulk-power supplier pending a re-tender, which may cast significant doubt on its ability to continue as a going concern. The auditor is satisfied with the accounting and the disclosure and does not regard Matter 2 as a basis for modifying the opinion.

Which of the following actions should the auditor take in framing the report?
1. Modify the opinion in respect of Matter 1 only, in the words 'except for the effects of matter described in Basis for Qualified Opinion section of our report'.
2. Report Matter 2 in a paragraph headed Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern, drawing attention to Note 27 and stating that the opinion is not modified in respect of that matter.
3. Amend the heading 'Basis for Opinion' to 'Basis for Qualified Opinion' and describe Matter 1 within that section.
4. State in the Opinion Paragraph that the FS do not give a true and fair view, because at least one departure from the framework has been established.
options: 1, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The two matters are different in character and are therefore reported in different places. Matter 1 is a known departure whose effect is confined, so the qualified extract applies, and with it the two obligations attaching to any modification - amending the basis heading to 'Basis for Qualified Opinion' and describing the matter giving rise to the modification within that section. Matter 2 is an appropriately recognised and disclosed material uncertainty, reported through the Going Concern paragraph containing the words 'material uncertainty exists that may cast significant doubt on company's ability to continue as going concern' and closing with the statement that the opinion is not modified. Action 4 states the adverse extract, which asserts that the FS as a whole do not give a true and fair view; a single confined departure does not support that, and the going concern matter has been disclosed and does not of itself modify the opinion.

questions.question:
Case: While reporting on the FS of Thanjavur Sugars Ltd for FY 2024-25, the auditor wishes to state in his report that the financial statements of one sugar unit, whose results are included in the figures he reports on, were audited by a different firm, that he has relied on that firm's report, and that he does not express an opinion on that unit's figures. Nothing on this is presented or disclosed as a matter of accounting in the FS, no uncertainty about the company's ability to continue is involved, and the auditor has obtained all the evidence he considers necessary for the balance of the FS and has identified no departure from the applicable financial reporting framework.

Which paragraph of the report is appropriate, and why?
options: An Other Matter paragraph, because the matter is not presented or disclosed in the FS and the paragraph is framed as a statement of the relevant matter followed by 'Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.'
An Emphasis of Matter paragraph, because the reliance placed on another auditor's report is a matter fundamental to users' understanding of the FS.
A disclaimer of opinion limited to the sugar unit, because the auditor states that he does not express an opinion on that unit's figures.
An adverse opinion on the FS, because part of the reported figures rests on another auditor's report rather than on work done by the reporting auditor himself.
questions.explanation: The Other Matter paragraph is the form framed for a matter relevant to the audit, to the auditor's responsibilities or to the report which is not something already presented or disclosed in the FS; its prescribed content is 'Relevant Matter. Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.' The Emphasis of Matter paragraph is unavailable because it is drafted as a draw of attention to a specified Note of the FS and the case states that no such disclosure exists. A disclaimer is a refusal to express an opinion on the FS themselves for inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence, which the case excludes by saying that the auditor obtained all evidence he considered necessary and found no departure; and an adverse opinion requires an affirmative conclusion that the FS do not give a true and fair view, which the auditor has not reached.

questions.category: SA 700 - Structure of the Opinion Extracts
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the structure of the four Opinion Paragraph extracts framed under a fair presentation framework:
1. Three, but only three, of the four extracts begin with 'In our opinion and to the best of our information and according to explanations given to us'.
2. Each of the qualified, adverse and disclaimer extracts contains a cross-reference to a specifically named section of the auditor's report.
3. The unmodified, qualified and adverse extracts each refer to the state of affairs of the entity as at March 31, 20XX and to its profit/loss and cash flows for the year ended on that date.
4. Only the disclaimer extract identifies the entity whose FS have been engaged to be audited and states that the auditor does not express an opinion.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1, 3 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 hold. The preamble appears in the unmodified, qualified and adverse extracts but not in the disclaimer extract; the qualified, adverse and disclaimer extracts each name their basis section - 'Basis for Qualified Opinion', 'Basis for Adverse Opinion', 'Basis for Disclaimer of Opinion'; and only the disclaimer extract opens with the engagement statement naming the entity and with the express refusal to express an opinion. Statement 3 fails on a single expression: the adverse extract refers to the financial position of the entity as at March 31, 20XX, while the unmodified and qualified extracts refer to the state of affairs of the entity. All three do refer to profit/loss and cash flows for the year ended on that date, which is what makes the statement read plausibly at speed.

questions.category: SA 700 - Report with Emphasis of Matter Only
questions.question:
Case: Punalur Ceramics Ltd is audited for FY 2024-25. The audit is completed with no departure from the applicable financial reporting framework and no limitation on the scope of the audit work, and the auditor's conclusion is that the FS give a true and fair view of the state of affairs of the entity as at March 31, 2025 and of its profit/loss and cash flows for the year ended on that date. The auditor nevertheless wishes to draw attention to Note 19, which describes the transfer of the company's manufacturing unit to a newly incorporated subsidiary during the year, considering it fundamental to users' understanding.

Which of the following statements are correct regarding the resulting report?
1. The Opinion Paragraph carries no 'except for', 'because of' or 'we do not express an opinion' construction.
2. The section headed 'Basis for Opinion' retains that heading and need not be renamed.
3. The Emphasis of Matter paragraph must state that the opinion is not modified in respect of the matter emphasised.
4. The unit transfer must be described within the Basis for Opinion section, because it is a matter reported in the audit report.
options: 1, 3 and 4 only
2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
questions.explanation: Because the opinion is unmodified, none of the qualifying constructions of the modified extracts appears, and the two obligations attached to a modification - amending the heading of the basis section and describing within it the matter giving rise to the modification - are not engaged at all, since the source attracts them only where the auditor modifies the opinion by qualification, adverse opinion or disclaimer. The Emphasis of Matter paragraph as framed necessarily carries the sentence 'Our opinion is not modified in respect of this matter', and the emphasised matter is taken up in that paragraph by reference to Note 19 rather than in the basis section. Statement 4 is the trap: it confuses the place where an emphasised matter is set out with the place where a matter giving rise to a modification of the opinion must be described.

questions.question:
Case: Kodaikanal Electronics Ltd is audited for FY 2024-25. The auditor has obtained complete evidence and finds that inventory of ₹940 crore is carried at cost while its realisable value is ₹210 crore, that no write-down has been recorded, and that the departure is compounded by the omission of the disclosures the framework requires in such a position. Total assets are ₹1,500 crore, net worth ₹620 crore and revenue ₹890 crore. The auditor concludes that the FS taken as a whole are incapable of giving a true and fair view and that reporting the matter as a mere exception would be inadequate. Management has refused to amend the FS. There is no limitation on the scope of the audit.

Which is the most appropriate report, and for what reason?
options: An adverse opinion, on the ground that because of omission of information / significance of the matter the FS do not give a true and fair view, the extract being worded by reference to the financial position of the entity as at March 31, 2025.
A disclaimer of opinion, because the effect of the misstatement is pervasive and the auditor cannot vouch for the balance of the FS once the largest asset is shown to be overstated.
A qualified opinion, because the matter is precisely quantifiable at ₹730 crore and anything capable of exact quantification can be reported as an exception.
An unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph, because management has been asked to amend the FS and its refusal to do so is itself the matter requiring emphasis.
questions.explanation: Two characteristics of the case are decisive. The auditor has full evidence, so the modification must express a conclusion on the FS rather than an inability to obtain evidence, which places the matter in the adverse opinion rather than the disclaimer; and his conclusion is that the FS taken as a whole do not give a true and fair view, which is beyond the reach of the 'except for the effects of' construction of a qualification even though the amount is precisely measurable - quantifiability fixes the description in the basis section, not the strength of the opinion. The adverse extract is drafted for exactly this position, using 'because of omission of information / significance of matter mentioned in Basis for Adverse Opinion section of our report' and referring to the financial position of the entity as at the balance sheet date. The Emphasis of Matter paragraph presupposes a matter appropriately presented or disclosed in the FS and states that the opinion is not modified, so it cannot carry a breach of that kind.

questions.category: SA 705 - Wording Analysis of the Qualified Extract
questions.question:
Case: Vidarbha Steel Ltd, an unlisted public company, prepares its financial statements in accordance with Ind AS, a financial reporting framework which requires compliance with its requirements and acknowledges that to achieve fair presentation of the FS management may provide disclosures beyond those specifically required. In the audit of FY 2024-25 the auditor, CA Rane & Associates, found that the company had neither recognised a liability of ₹148 crore for environmental remediation ordered by the National Green Tribunal nor disclosed the matter in the notes to the FS. Management agreed that no provision had been made and that no note had been written, and the auditor concluded that this was a departure from the requirements of the applicable financial reporting framework. The matter was material, but its effect was confined to the said liability, the omitted disclosure, the consequential tax effect and the resulting overstatement of profit; the remaining elements of the FS were, in the auditor's judgment, still capable of being read as giving a true and fair view but for that matter. There was no limitation on the scope of the audit and the auditor had obtained complete evidence about the NGT order and the amount involved.

Which of the following statements about the wording of the Opinion Paragraph in this report are correct?
1. The extract preserves the standard preamble and still asserts that the FS give a true and fair view, so an affirmative conclusion on the FS survives.
2. The qualifying clause must name the section of the report in which the matter giving rise to the modification is described.
3. The qualifying clause for this situation is introduced by the words 'because of'.
4. The extract refers to the state of affairs of the entity as at March 31, 2025 and to its profit/loss and cash flows for the year ended on that date.
options: 1, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: A qualified opinion is a modified opinion in which the affirmation survives and is cut down only by the exception, so statement 1 is right; and the exception is expressed by reference to the section where the matter is described - 'except for the effects of matter described in Basis for Qualified Opinion section of our report' - which makes statement 2 right and ties the Opinion Paragraph to the amended heading. Statement 3 is wrong because 'because of' introduces the qualifying clause of the adverse and disclaimer extracts, not of the qualified extract; using it would put before the reader the conclusion that the FS do not give a true and fair view. Statement 4 follows the unmodified and qualified wording, which speaks of the state of affairs of the entity; the adverse extract alone substitutes financial position, which is the marker that distinguishes it from the qualified extract besides the 'except for' / 'because of' contrast.

questions.category: SA 705 - Basis for Opinion Heading - Assertion Reason
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Where an audit report contains an Emphasis of Matter paragraph or a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern paragraph but the auditor's opinion is unmodified, the heading 'Basis for Opinion' is not amended.
Reason (R): The requirement to amend the heading to 'Basis for Qualified Opinion', 'Basis for Adverse Opinion' or 'Basis for Disclaimer of Opinion' and to include within that section a description of the matter giving rise to it is attracted only when the auditor modifies the opinion on the FS.
In the context of the above, which of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation: The source conditions both limbs of the basis-section requirement on the auditor modifying the opinion, and it identifies the modifications as qualification, adverse opinion and disclaimer. An Emphasis of Matter paragraph and a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern paragraph each close with the express statement that the opinion is not modified in respect of the matter, so neither attracts the amendment of the heading; A is therefore a direct consequence of the condition stated in R, and R is the explanation rather than a merely coincident rule. A candidate who treats the addition of any paragraph to the report as a trigger for renaming the basis section has misread the scope of the requirement, which is keyed to modification of the opinion and not to the presence of extra paragraphs in the report.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the matters on which an auditor has a duty to inquire under section 143(1) of the Companies Act, 2013:
1. The auditor must inquire whether loans and advances made on the basis of security have been properly secured and whether their terms are prejudicial to the interests of the company or its members.
2. The auditor must inquire whether transactions represented merely by book entries are prejudicial to the interests of the company.
3. The auditor must inquire into securities sold below cost under section 143(1)(c) even where the company is an investment company or a banking company.
4. The auditor must inquire whether personal expenses have been charged to the revenue account.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 2, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Section 143(1) sets out an exhaustive list of inquiries, and statements 1, 2 and 4 correctly reproduce limbs (a), (b) and (e) of that list. Statement 3 is wrong because limb (c) applies only where the company is not an investment company and not a banking company; for such companies the below-cost sale of shares, debentures and other securities is expressly outside the inquiry. The decisive condition is the investment/banking-company carve-out in limb (c). Any option that admits statement 3 therefore misstates the provision and must be rejected.

questions.question:
Match each limb of section 143(1) in Column I with the matter it requires the auditor to inquire into in Column II.
Column I:
P. Limb (a)
Q. Limb (b)
R. Limb (c)
S. Limb (f)
Column II:
1. Whether loans and advances made by the company have been shown as deposits.
2. Whether loans and advances made on the basis of security have been properly secured and whether their terms are prejudicial to the interests of the company or its members.
3. Where the company, not being an investment company or a banking company, whether shares, debentures and other securities have been sold at a price less than the purchase price.
4. Whether transactions of the company represented merely by book entries are prejudicial to the interests of the company.
5. Where the books state that shares have been allotted for cash, whether cash has actually been received.
questions.explanation: Limb (a) maps to Column-II item 2, limb (b) to item 4, limb (c) to item 3 and limb (f) to item 5, so the pairing (a)-2, (b)-4, (c)-3, (f)-5 is the only fully correct one. Item 1 (loans and advances shown as deposits) is limb (d) and is a deliberate distractor that is not asked for, so options assigning (c)-1 or (f)-1 are wrong. The candidate must place the below-cost sale of securities in limb (c) and the share-allotment-for-cash inquiry in limb (f). Confusing limb (c) with limb (d), or limb (f) with limb (c), produces the other options.

questions.question:
Case Study. M/s Kalyani & Associates are the statutory auditors of Udupi Processing Ltd, a public company engaged in cashew processing (it is neither an investment company nor a banking company), for the financial year 2024-25. During the audit the following facts emerge:
1. The company granted an unsecured loan of ₹2 crore to M/s Ganesh Traders, a firm in which a director is a partner, at interest of 4%, below the company's own cost of borrowing.
2. The company sold 15,000 equity shares of a listed company, which it had purchased two years earlier at ₹220 each, for ₹150 each.
3. The company recorded a sale of goods worth ₹45 lakh to a buyer; no goods actually moved, the transaction is represented merely by book entries, and its terms operate against the company's interest.
4. The managing director's family wedding expenses of ₹8 lakh were debited to the statement of profit and loss.
5. Shares aggregating ₹50 lakh were recorded in the books as allotted for cash during the year, but the bank records show that no such cash was actually received.
6. The auditor further finds that the financial statements do not comply with one applicable Accounting Standard.
Which of the numbered facts fall within the auditor's duty to INQUIRE under section 143(1) of the Companies Act, 2013?
options: 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 only
2, 3, 4 and 5 only
1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 only
questions.explanation: Section 143(1) enumerates the duty to inquire and covers facts 1 to 5: a loan on prejudicial terms (limb (a)), securities sold below cost by a company that is neither an investment nor a banking company (limb (c)), a transaction represented merely by book entries (limb (b)), personal expenses charged to revenue (limb (e)) and shares shown as allotted for cash although no cash was received (limb (f)). Fact 6, non-compliance with an Accounting Standard, is not a 143(1) inquiry; it is a separate duty to report under section 143(3)(e). The decisive point is the boundary between the exhaustive 143(1) inquiry list and the 143(3) reporting duties. Dropping fact 2 (a valid limb-(c) inquiry here) or pulling in fact 6 both misclassify the provisions.

questions.question:
Case Study. M/s Kalyani & Associates are the statutory auditors of Udupi Processing Ltd, a public company engaged in cashew processing (it is neither an investment company nor a banking company), for the financial year 2024-25. During the audit the following facts emerge:
1. The company granted an unsecured loan of ₹2 crore to M/s Ganesh Traders, a firm in which a director is a partner, at interest of 4%, below the company's own cost of borrowing.
2. The company sold 15,000 equity shares of a listed company, which it had purchased two years earlier at ₹220 each, for ₹150 each.
3. The company recorded a sale of goods worth ₹45 lakh to a buyer; no goods actually moved, the transaction is represented merely by book entries, and its terms operate against the company's interest.
4. The managing director's family wedding expenses of ₹8 lakh were debited to the statement of profit and loss.
5. Shares aggregating ₹50 lakh were recorded in the books as allotted for cash during the year, but the bank records show that no such cash was actually received.
6. The auditor further finds that the financial statements do not comply with one applicable Accounting Standard.
The following statements are made about facts 1, 3 and 4:
1. Fact 1 engages limb (a), which permits inquiry into whether the terms of the loan are prejudicial to the interests of the company or of its members.
2. Fact 3 engages limb (b), because the transaction is represented merely by book entries.
3. Because limb (a) speaks only of the company's interest, fact 1 can be reported only if the loan prejudices the company and not merely its members.
4. Fact 4 engages limb (e), which concerns personal expenses charged to the revenue account.
Which of these statements are correct?
options: 1, 2 and 4 only
2 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statement 1 correctly captures limb (a), which extends to terms prejudicial to the interests of the company or its members, so statement 3, which wrongly restricts limb (a) to the company's interest alone and drops the words "or its members", is the incorrect one. Statement 2 is correct: a transaction represented merely by book entries falls under limb (b). Statement 4 is correct: personal expenses charged to the revenue account fall under limb (e). The decisive fact is that limb (a) expressly covers the interest of the members as well as the company. Any option admitting statement 3 (the "all four" option or the 1-3-4 option) is therefore wrong.

questions.question:
Case Study. M/s Kalyani & Associates are the statutory auditors of Udupi Processing Ltd, a public company engaged in cashew processing (it is neither an investment company nor a banking company), for the financial year 2024-25. During the audit the following facts emerge:
1. The company granted an unsecured loan of ₹2 crore to M/s Ganesh Traders, a firm in which a director is a partner, at interest of 4%, below the company's own cost of borrowing.
2. The company sold 15,000 equity shares of a listed company, which it had purchased two years earlier at ₹220 each, for ₹150 each.
3. The company recorded a sale of goods worth ₹45 lakh to a buyer; no goods actually moved, the transaction is represented merely by book entries, and its terms operate against the company's interest.
4. The managing director's family wedding expenses of ₹8 lakh were debited to the statement of profit and loss.
5. Shares aggregating ₹50 lakh were recorded in the books as allotted for cash during the year, but the bank records show that no such cash was actually received.
6. The auditor further finds that the financial statements do not comply with one applicable Accounting Standard.
Regarding fact 5 (shares recorded as allotted for cash though no cash received), what must the auditor determine and, if the answer is adverse, report under limb (f) of section 143(1)?
options: Whether the stated allotment for cash was in fact a benami transaction.
Whether the shares were issued at a discount permitted under the Companies Act.
Whether the allotment was approved by a special resolution of the members.
Whether cash was actually received and, if not, whether the position stated in the books and balance sheet is correct, regular and not misleading.
questions.explanation: Limb (f) is triggered only where the books or documents state that shares have been allotted for cash; the auditor must then inquire whether cash was actually received and, if it was not, whether the position as stated in the account books and the balance sheet is correct, regular and not misleading. On fact 5 the bank records show no cash received, so the answer is adverse and the misleading position must be reported. The rule is confined to the truth of the "allotted for cash" statement; inquiries into benami status, into issue at a discount, or into the mode of shareholder approval fall outside limb (f) and are not the applicable test.

questions.question: The statutory auditors of Kakinada Holdings Ltd, a public company, for FY 2024-25 note that the company sold listed equity shares it had earlier purchased at a price below their purchase price; that a ₹3 crore unsecured loan was given to a director's firm on below-market terms; and that a director's personal expenses were charged to revenue. Kakinada's principal business is the acquisition and holding of securities and it is an investment company. If Kakinada were NOT an investment company, which of these findings would newly attract a section 143(1) inquiry?
options: Both the below-cost share sale and the unsecured loan to the director's firm
The below-cost sale of listed equity shares only
The unsecured loan to the director's firm only
The director's personal expenses charged to revenue only
questions.explanation: Section 143(1)(c) requires an inquiry into assets consisting of shares, debentures and other securities sold below purchase price only where the company is not an investment company or a banking company; because Kakinada is an investment company that limb does not operate, and it would newly bite only if Kakinada ceased to be one. The loan on unsecured, prejudicial terms is covered by limb (a) and the personal expenses by limb (e), and both apply to every company regardless of investment-company status, so removing that status would not newly bring them in. The decisive fact is the investment-company carve-out confined to limb (c).

questions.question: M/s Kalyani & Associates audit Udupi Processing Ltd (neither an investment nor a banking company) for FY 2024-25. They record a sale of goods worth ₹45 lakh represented merely by book entries with no goods movement; on examination the terms of this book-entry transaction are found to be at arm's length and in no way prejudicial to the company. Under section 143(1), what should the auditor do about this book-entry transaction?
options: Refuse to report anything, because the auditor need not report under 143(1) unless he finds the answer to any matter in the adverse.
Report it under limb (b) because any book-entry-only transaction must be reported.
Report it under section 143(3)(f) as an observation on financial transactions.
Report it under limb (d) as a loan shown as a deposit.
questions.explanation: Limb (b) inquires whether transactions represented merely by book entries are prejudicial to the interests of the company; here the transaction is not prejudicial, so the answer to the inquiry is favourable, not adverse. The Note to section 143(1) provides that the auditor is not required to report on these matters unless he finds the answer to any of them in the adverse, so there is nothing to report. A rule that every book-entry transaction must be reported is therefore wrong, and this is neither a section 143(3)(f) matter, which concerns an adverse effect on the functioning of the company, nor a loans-shown-as-deposits matter under limb (d). The decisive condition is the "only if adverse" trigger.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Note to section 143(1):
1. The auditor must make the inquiries under every limb of section 143(1) in every audit.
2. The auditor is required to report a 143(1) matter only when he finds the answer to it in the adverse.
3. Because reporting is only if adverse, the auditor need not inquire into a matter unless he suspects it will be adverse.
4. The Note removes the obligation to report 143(1) matters that turn out favourably, but the inquiry itself is still performed.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 2 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Section 143(1) imposes a duty to inquire on all the listed matters in every audit, so statement 1 is correct, and the Note only qualifies the duty to report, which arises when the answer is adverse, making statements 2 and 4 correct. Statement 4 is the precise articulation of this: the inquiry is performed but favourable results are not reported. Statement 3 is wrong because inquiring only when an adverse answer is suspected would nullify the very duty to inquire - the statute requires the inquiry first and reporting only if the answer turns out adverse. Hence 1, 2 and 4 are correct; any option admitting statement 3 is rejected.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about section 143(1). Which are NOT correct?
