P, R, Q, T, S
questions.explanation: The clause opens with the regularity question for undisputed dues, which logically precedes any arrear computation. The next filter is whether a dispute exists, because a mere representation keeps the amount in the undisputed stream while a genuine dispute routes it away from the arrear figure. Only then is the outstanding position struck as on the last day of the financial year, and only after that can the six-month period from the due date be applied to that struck balance. Disputed amounts are finally disclosed with the forum. Any sequence which applies the six-month test before the outstanding position is fixed, or which routes an amount to the dispute disclosure before deciding whether a dispute exists, cannot produce the clause's result.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A statutory due which was unpaid on 31st March of the year under report for only five months from its due date is not to be indicated as arrears under clause (vii)(a) of CARO, 2020, even if it continues to remain unpaid for nine months by the time the audit report is signed.
Reason (R): Clause (vii)(a) requires the arrears of outstanding statutory dues to be ascertained as on the last day of the financial year concerned, with the period of more than six months reckoned from the due date.
Which of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
questions.explanation: The assertion follows directly from the two conditions in the clause: the outstanding position is frozen as on the last day of the financial year, and the qualifying period is more than six months from the due date. Since only five months had run from the due date by that reference date, the amount is not indicated as arrears, and events between the year-end and the date of the report do not alter the measurement. The reason states exactly the conditions which produce the assertion, so it is not merely true but is the explanation of it. A is not wrong, because no rule extends the arrear test to the report date, and R is not wrong, because it reproduces the clause's own reference points.

questions.question:
Case study: Nandyal Agro Products Ltd., for FY 2024-25, is a company to which CARO, 2020 applies. Each of the following is independently substantiated, and the company has no other borrowings:
(1) A term loan of ₹ 40 crore was sanctioned in March 2024 by Punjab National Bank exclusively for commissioning a bio-solvent plant. In April 2024 the company deployed ₹ 11 crore of it to acquire a 26 per cent stake in its associate Kistha Oils Pvt Ltd.
(2) A working capital limit of ₹ 15 crore, being short-term bank finance repayable on demand, was drawn in June 2024 and ₹ 12 crore of it was used to purchase plant and machinery and to meet the civil construction cost of a new warehouse.
(3) To enable its wholly-owned subsidiary to redeem ₹ 6 crore of debentures maturing on 31.03.2025, the company received ₹ 6 crore during January 2025 from an unrelated trading company under an unregistered inter-corporate arrangement, and passed it on to the subsidiary.
(4) A loan of ₹ 9 crore was drawn from Anantha Urban Co-operative Bank Ltd, secured by pledge of shares which the company holds in its joint venture Guntur Bagasse Pvt Ltd. The quarterly interest instalment of ₹ 17 lakh due on 15.12.2024 was paid only on 24.01.2025.
(5) On redeemable non-convertible debentures of ₹ 20 crore, the interest instalment of ₹ 15 lakh due on 31.12.2024 remained unpaid for 12 days.
(6) Union Bank of India recorded the company as a wilful defaulter in February 2025 in respect of a previously restructured working capital account; the company has approached the Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunal against that recording.
(7) Payments to trade creditors for raw material were delayed by an average of 34 days beyond credit terms, and two export-processing dues were also paid after the due date.
Match the facts with the sub-clauses of clause (ix) of CARO, 2020:
Sub-clauses:
(a) default in repayment of loans or other borrowings or in payment of interest to any lender
(b) declared a wilful defaulter by any bank or financial institution
(c) whether term loans were applied for the purpose for which they were obtained
(d) funds raised on a short-term basis utilised for long-term purposes
(e) funds taken from any entity or person to meet obligations of subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures
(f) loans raised on pledge of securities held in subsidiaries, joint ventures or associate companies
Which pairing is correct?
questions.explanation: Fact 1 is deployment of term loan proceeds on an object other than the one for which the loan was obtained, which is clause (ix)(c). Fact 2 is utilisation of short-term working capital finance for plant, machinery and building, that is, funds raised on a short-term basis applied to long-term purposes, which is clause (ix)(d). Fact 3 is money taken in by the company from another entity to discharge an obligation of its subsidiary, which is clause (ix)(e). Fact 4 is a loan raised on the pledge of securities held in a joint venture, so clause (ix)(f) applies, and because the interest on that very loan was paid 40 days late, clause (ix)(a) applies to it as well. Fact 5 is unpaid interest on debt securities owed to debenture holders, a default to a lender under clause (ix)(a), and fact 6 is a declaration by a bank, which is clause (ix)(b).

(1) A term loan of ₹ 40 crore was sanctioned in March 2024 by Punjab National Bank exclusively for commissioning a bio-solvent plant. In April 2024 the company deployed ₹ 11 crore of it to acquire a 26 per cent stake in its associate Kistha Oils Pvt Ltd.
(2) A working capital limit of ₹ 15 crore, being short-term bank finance repayable on demand, was drawn in June 2024 and ₹ 12 crore of it was used to purchase plant and machinery and to meet the civil construction cost of a new warehouse.
(3) To enable its wholly-owned subsidiary to redeem ₹ 6 crore of debentures maturing on 31.03.2025, the company received ₹ 6 crore during January 2025 from an unrelated trading company under an unregistered inter-corporate arrangement, and passed it on to the subsidiary.
(4) A loan of ₹ 9 crore was drawn from Anantha Urban Co-operative Bank Ltd, secured by pledge of shares which the company holds in its joint venture Guntur Bagasse Pvt Ltd. The quarterly interest instalment of ₹ 17 lakh due on 15.12.2024 was paid only on 24.01.2025.
(5) On redeemable non-convertible debentures of ₹ 20 crore, the interest instalment of ₹ 15 lakh due on 31.12.2024 remained unpaid for 12 days.
(6) Union Bank of India recorded the company as a wilful defaulter in February 2025 in respect of a previously restructured working capital account; the company has approached the Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunal against that recording.
(7) Payments to trade creditors for raw material were delayed by an average of 34 days beyond credit terms, and two export-processing dues were also paid after the due date.
Which of the following statements are correct?
1. A default in payment of interest has to be reported under clause (ix)(a) in respect of both fact 4 and fact 5, because the clause covers loans or other borrowings and interest owed to any lender and prescribes no minimum number of days.
2. Fact 7 is also reportable under clause (ix)(a), because trade creditors extending credit are lenders of goods.
3. Clause (ix)(f) requires not only details of the loan raised against the pledge of the joint venture shares but also whether the company has defaulted in repayment of that loan.
4. Clause (ix)(b) is answered in the negative so long as the company's challenge to the wilful-defaulter recording is pending before the appellate tribunal.
options: 2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1, 3 and 4 only
1 and 3 only
questions.explanation: Clause (ix)(a) asks only whether there has been default in repayment of loans or other borrowings or in payment of interest to any lender, and its format calls for the number of days of delay or unpaid, so neither a 40-day nor a 12-day default can be excluded. Clause (ix)(f) is drafted in two parts and both must be answered. Fact 7 concerns trade payables, which are neither loans or borrowings nor interest payable to a lender, and the delayed export-processing dues belong to clause (vii), not clause (ix). Clause (ix)(b) turns on the single fact of a declaration by a bank or financial institution, which Union Bank of India has made; the clause contains no qualification for a declaration under challenge. Statements 1 and 3 are therefore the only correct ones.

(7) Payments to trade creditors for raw material were delayed by an average of 34 days beyond credit terms, and two export-processing dues were also paid after the due date.
While completing the prescribed format under clause (ix)(a) for the default described in fact 4, which set of entries is correct?
options: Nature of borrowing: loan secured by pledge of shares; Name of lender: Anantha Urban Co-operative Bank Ltd; Amount not paid on due date: ₹ 9 crore; Whether principal or interest: interest; Number of days of delay or unpaid: 40; Remarks: nil.

Nature of borrowing: loan secured by pledge of shares held in the joint venture; Name of lender: Anantha Urban Co-operative Bank Ltd; Amount not paid on due date: ₹ 17 lakh; Whether principal or interest: interest; Number of days of delay or unpaid: 40; Remarks: nil, the instalment having been cleared on 24.01.2025.

Nature of borrowing: term loan sanctioned for commissioning the bio-solvent plant; Name of lender: Punjab National Bank; Amount not paid on due date: ₹ 9 crore, being the amount sanctioned; Whether principal or interest: principal; Number of days of delay or unpaid: 15; Remarks: nil.

Nature of borrowing: debt securities; Name of lender: the debenture holders; Amount not paid on due date: ₹ 17 lakh; Whether principal or interest: interest; Number of days of delay or unpaid: 12; Remarks: paid after the due date.
questions.explanation: The format columns become self-explaining once the facts are mapped. The borrowing is a loan obtained against the pledge of shares held in the joint venture, so the nature-of-borrowing column must carry that security character; the lender is the co-operative bank which advanced ₹ 9 crore; and the amount which was not paid on the due date of 15.12.2024 is the interest instalment of ₹ 17 lakh, not the principal sanctioned. The 'whether principal or interest' column takes the character of the defaulted sum, and the delay from 15.12.2024 to 24.01.2025 is 40 days. The distractors either borrow figures from the other facts, treat the whole sanctioned amount as unpaid when no principal had fallen due, or attribute the debenture facts of fact 5 to the pledged-share loan.

(4) A loan of ₹ 9 crore was drawn from Anantha Urban Co-operative Bank Ltd, secured by pledge of shares which the company holds in its joint venture Guntur Bagasse Pvt Ltd. The quarterly interest instalment of ₹ 17 lakh due on 15.12.2024 was paid only on 24.01.2025.
(5) On redeemable non-convertible debentures of ₹ 20 crore, the interest instalment of ₹ 15 lakh due on 31.12.2024 remained unpaid for 12 days.
(6) Union Bank of India recorded the company as a wilful defaulter in February 2025 in respect of a previously restructured working capital account; the company has approached the Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunal against that recording.
(7) Payments to trade creditors for raw material were delayed by an average of 34 days beyond credit terms, and two export-processing dues were also paid after the due date.
The finance head objects that the 12-day delay in paying ₹ 15 lakh of debenture interest is too small to report and that clause (ix)(a) is confined to defaults in favour of banks and financial institutions. Which conclusion should the auditor reach?
options: The objection is unsound, but the debenture interest is reported under clause (ix)(f), that being the only sub-clause of clause (ix) which deals with debt securities and with payments to holders of instruments.

The objection is sound only as to quantum, because a delay of twelve days in paying interest is not a default in repayment of loans or borrowings, the clause being confined to principal which has fallen due and remains unpaid.

The objection is sound on both counts, because clause (ix)(a) contemplates only institutional lenders such as banks and financial institutions, and a delay of less than a month in servicing a coupon is not material enough to be reported in the format.

The objection is unsound: the clause covers loans or other borrowings and payment of interest to any lender, its format expressly contemplates debt securities, and no minimum period of default is prescribed.
questions.explanation: Clause (ix)(a) is framed by reference to 'any lender' and to default in repayment of loans or other borrowings or in the payment of interest, and the first column of its format is 'nature of borrowing, including debt securities', which brings debentures and bonds within it alongside bank borrowings. The clause prescribes no waiting period; the number of days of delay or unpaid is exactly what the format requires to be stated, so 12 days is reported as 12 days. Clause (ix)(f) deals with loans raised on the pledge of securities held in subsidiaries, joint ventures or associates and has nothing to do with debentures, and a partial answer which concedes the institutional-lender point would still be wrong.

(7) Payments to trade creditors for raw material were delayed by an average of 34 days beyond credit terms, and two export-processing dues were also paid after the due date.
Which of the following actions should the auditor take in relation to clause (ix)?
options: Avoid reporting fact 6 because the recording is still under challenge before the appellate tribunal, and avoid reporting fact 5 because the delay in paying debenture interest was only 12 days and is not a default in repayment of borrowings.

Report the ₹ 11 crore diverted from the term loan under clause (ix)(d) as funds used for a long-term purpose, report the working capital utilisation under clause (ix)(c) as a term loan applied for an unintended purpose, and confine the format under clause (ix)(a) to defaults in repayment of principal, stating the period of each such default.

Treat fact 3 as a loan granted by the company to its subsidiary and disclose it under clause (ix)(e) as such, exclude the co-operative bank borrowing from clause (ix)(f) because the pledged securities were of a joint venture and not of a subsidiary, and omit fact 5 on the ground that debenture holders are not lenders.

Quantify the ₹ 11 crore of term loan proceeds applied to the associate stake together with the purpose of such use; indicate the nature and amount of the short-term funds used for long-term purposes; give details of the ₹ 6 crore received to meet the subsidiary's obligation with the nature of that transaction; and report the pledged-share loan and the default on it.
questions.explanation: Each sub-clause of clause (ix) calls for a distinct piece of work: (c) needs the amount of the term loan diverted and the purpose for which it was used, (d) needs the nature and amount of short-term funds utilised for long-term purposes, (e) needs the details of funds taken from another entity to meet a subsidiary's obligation with the nature of the transaction and the amount in each case, and (f) needs the details of the loan raised on pledge of securities held in a joint venture together with any default in repaying it. The ₹ 11 crore belongs to (c) and not (d), and the working capital utilisation belongs to (d) and not (c), while (a) covers interest as well as principal. Fact 3 records money received rather than advanced, and (f) expressly extends to joint ventures and associates as well as subsidiaries.

(7) Payments to trade creditors for raw material were delayed by an average of 34 days beyond credit terms, and two export-processing dues were also paid after the due date.
Counsel for the company argues that clause (ix)(e) cannot apply because Nandyal did not grant any loan to its subsidiary; it merely received money from a third party and discharged the subsidiary's debenture obligation. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?
options: The argument is irrelevant, because every movement of funds between the company and its subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures is reportable under clause (ix)(c) as an application of funds, whatever its direction.

The argument is correct in substance, but the fact must still be reported under clause (ix)(f), because funds applied for the benefit of a group company are treated as raised on the security of the group holdings.

The argument is irrelevant: clause (ix)(e) is engaged by the company taking funds from any entity or person to meet the obligations of its subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures, and the details, the nature of such transactions and the amount in each case must be given.

The argument is correct, because clause (ix)(e) presupposes a loan or advance granted by the company to its subsidiary, associate or joint venture, and since Nandyal granted no loan, nor gave any guarantee or security in that transaction, nothing arises for disclosure.
questions.explanation: Clause (ix)(e) is directed at funds which the company takes in from any entity or person in order to meet the obligations of its subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures; the inflow, and not an outflow, is the trigger, and the disclosure extends to the details, the nature of such transactions and the amount in each case. Nandyal received ₹ 6 crore from an unrelated trading company and applied it to the subsidiary's debenture redemption, which is squarely within the clause. Clause (ix)(f) concerns loans raised on the pledge of securities held in group companies, and clause (ix)(c) concerns application of term loans for the purposes for which they were obtained, so neither can host this fact. The contention mistakes clause (ix)(e) for the mirror image of the lending provisions.

Regarding fact 6, which of the following statements is correct about reporting under clause (ix)(b)?
options: It is answered in the affirmative only if the same account is also reported as a default in the format under clause (ix)(a).
It is answered in the negative because the recording arises from a restructured working capital account rather than from a term loan.

It is answered in the affirmative, because the sub-clause asks whether the company has been declared a wilful defaulter by any bank or financial institution and such a recording has been made by a bank.

It is answered in the negative so long as the company's appeal against the recording is pending before the appellate tribunal, because a declaration which stands under judicial challenge cannot be treated as a final declaration.
questions.explanation: Clause (ix)(b) is a single-fact enquiry as to whether the company has been declared a wilful defaulter by any bank or financial institution. Union Bank of India is a bank and has made that recording, so the answer is affirmative and is reported as such. The sub-clause is not confined to any class of facility, so the fact that the recording arises from a restructured working capital account does not exclude it, and it is drafted independently of clause (ix)(a), so no contemporaneous format entry is a precondition. The source contains no qualification for a declaration which the company is contesting before an appellate forum.
