The manipulation was reversed in the audited financial statements at the instance of the statutory auditor.
(3) Three complaints were received during the year under the company's vigil mechanism. The Audit Committee inquired into them and recorded in its minutes that two were not substantiated and that one was partly substantiated. The statutory auditor did not read the complaints or the records of inquiry, taking the view that the vigil mechanism is the concern of the Audit Committee.
(4) The statutory auditor filed with the Central Government a report under section 143(12) of the Companies Act, 2013 in Form ADT-4 in respect of the matter described in paragraph (1).

Which of the following statements about CARO clause (xi), read with the above case, are NOT correct?
1. Clause (xi)(a) is answered only in respect of a fraud which remains uncorrected at the balance sheet date, so the reversal of the fictitious export sales takes paragraph (2) outside the clause.
2. Clause (xi) requires the auditor to consider whistle-blower complaints received by the company in addition to any fraud noticed or reported during the year.
3. Paragraphs (1) and (2) each require the nature and the amount involved to be indicated.
4. Clause (xi)(b) requires the auditor to state whether he had reason to believe that an offence of fraud had been committed, whether or not any report was filed.
Which of the above statements are NOT correct?
options: 1 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3 only
3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is not correct, because clause (xi)(a) is triggered by fraud noticed or reported during the year and contains no requirement that the fraud remain uncorrected at the year end; the reversal of ₹9.6 crore of fictitious export sales is relevant to the financial statements, not to whether the fraud is reported. Statement 4 is not correct, because clause (xi)(b) asks whether a report under section 143(12) has been filed by the auditors in Form ADT-4 with the Central Government, which is a statement about a filing and not about the auditor's reason to believe. Statements 2 and 3 are correct readings of limbs (c) and (a) respectively, and it is the co-existence of three distinct limbs within clause (xi) which the two incorrect statements each collapse into one.

questions.question:
CASE STUDY: Nalanda Pharma Limited, an unlisted public company, has a financial year ending 31 March 2025. It operates through 42 branches and two manufacturing units and reported revenue of ₹1,850 crore for the year. The following matters were ascertained during the audit:
(1) The company entered into eleven transactions with related parties during the year. The auditor ascertained that the requirements of section 188 of the Companies Act, 2013 had been complied with in respect of all the eleven transactions, but that the requirements of section 177 had not been complied with in respect of two of them. The notes to the accounts contained the disclosures required by the applicable accounting standard for all the eleven transactions.
(2) Before the audit report was signed, the two transactions referred to above were placed before the Audit Committee, which ratified them; the statutory auditor noted this in his working papers.
(3) The company transferred a commercial building with a written down value of ₹9 crore to its managing director as consideration for the equity shares held by him in a subsidiary, no cash passing between the parties. The auditor was satisfied that the requirements of section 192 of the Companies Act, 2013 had been complied with.
(4) The company purchased packaging material worth ₹2.4 crore for cash during the year from a proprietary concern of the sister of its chief executive director. The price was settled by electronic transfer and the transaction is included in the related party disclosures in the notes.
(5) The company has an internal audit department of four officers which reports quarterly to the Audit Committee, covers the two manufacturing units annually and has not visited any branch for three years. The statutory auditor obtained a written representation from the chief financial officer that the internal audit system was adequate, and neither obtained nor read any internal audit report.
(6) The statutory auditor was appointed in 2023 for a five year term, and the fee of the internal audit department is debited to the operating cost centres.

Based on the above case, which of the following statements are correct with respect to CARO clause (xiii)?
1. The compliance limb of clause (xiii) is answered in the negative, because section 177 was not complied with in respect of two of the eleven transactions, and the affirmative position under section 188 for all eleven does not change that answer.
2. Clause (xiii) calls for one composite answer and cannot be split between compliance with sections 177 and 188 on the one hand and disclosure of the details in the financial statements as per the applicable accounting standards on the other.
3. Clause (xiii) calls for an examination of all transactions with related parties, so the auditor cannot confine his test to transactions which appear material individually or in aggregate.
4. Whether the related party disclosures in the notes are adequate is tested by clause (xiii) against the applicable accounting standards.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
1, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Clause (xiii) carries two requirements — that all transactions with related parties are in compliance with sections 177 and 188 of the Companies Act, 2013, and that the details have been disclosed in the financial statements as per the applicable accounting standards — and each has to be answered, which is why the statement claiming a single indivisible answer fails. On these facts the disclosure requirement is satisfied while the section 177 requirement is not, and a single failure of compliance is enough to make the compliance answer negative, so statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 follows from the words 'all transactions with related parties'; and the ratification by the Audit Committee before the report was signed, recorded in paragraph (2), is a fact for the working papers which does not alter the clause (xiii) enquiry into whether all the transactions of the year were in compliance.

The statutory auditor obtained a written representation from the chief financial officer that the internal audit system was adequate, and neither obtained nor read any internal audit report.
(6) The statutory auditor was appointed in 2023 for a five year term, and the fee of the internal audit department is debited to the operating cost centres.

Which of the following correctly states the treatment of the transactions described in paragraphs (3) and (4) of the above case under CARO clause (xv)?
options: Both transactions fall within clause (xv), because that clause is drawn widely enough to take in every transaction which the company enters into either with one of its directors or with a person connected with one of its directors, and both counterparties here answer that description.

Only the building against shares transaction is within clause (xv), and for it the auditor reports that section 192 of the Companies Act, 2013 has been complied with, while the cash purchase from the sister's proprietary concern is outside clause (xv) but remains within clause (xiii).

Only the cash purchase of packaging material is within clause (xv), because section 192 is attracted whenever the company parts with money or with any other benefit in favour of a person connected with one of its directors, the mode by which the price happens to be settled being immaterial for the purpose.

Neither transaction is within clause (xv), because that clause covers only transactions which the company enters into with its own directors personally and does not reach transactions entered into with persons who are connected with those directors.
questions.explanation: Clause (xv) is confined to non-cash transactions with directors or persons connected with him, and where the company has entered into such a transaction the auditor has to state whether the provisions of section 192 of the Companies Act, 2013 have been complied with. The transfer of a building of ₹9 crore written down value to the managing director against shares is a non-cash transaction with a director and is reported under the clause together with the auditor's satisfaction on section 192; the ₹2.4 crore purchase settled by electronic transfer is a cash transaction and so falls outside clause (xv), though the counterparty being the sister of a director keeps it within clause (xiii). The answer sweeping both transactions in ignores the qualifier non-cash, the answer excluding both ignores the words 'or persons connected with him', and the answer resting on the transfer of a benefit substitutes a test the clause does not use for the absence of cash which is the actual test.

(4) The company purchased packaging material worth ₹2.4 crore for cash during the year from a proprietary concern of the sister of its chief executive director. The price was settled by electronic transfer and the transaction is included in the related party disclosures in the notes.

(6) The statutory auditor was appointed in 2023 for a five year term, and the fee of the internal audit department is debited to the operating cost centres.

Which of the following actions should the statutory auditor take with respect to CARO clause (xiv) in the above case?
1. Assess whether the internal audit system is commensurate with the size and the nature of the company's business, treating the absence of any branch visit for three years as relevant to that assessment.
2. Obtain and read the internal audit reports for the year, and, since he has not done so, refrain from stating under clause (xiv)(b) that the reports of the internal auditors were considered by him.
3. Rely on the chief financial officer's written representation as a sufficient basis for the clause (xiv)(a) answer, since the adequacy of the internal audit system is a matter of management judgment.
4. Treat the two limbs of clause (xiv) as independent, so that a satisfactory conclusion on the existence of an internal audit system does not by itself answer the question whether the internal auditors' reports were considered.
Which of the above actions should be taken?
options: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Clause (xiv) asks two things — whether the company has an internal audit system commensurate with the size and nature of its business, and whether the reports of the internal auditors were considered by the statutory auditor. A company with ₹1,850 crore of revenue, 42 branches and two manufacturing units whose four member internal audit department has not visited a branch for three years requires that coverage gap to be analysed against both size and nature, so action 1 is called for; the auditor has neither obtained nor read an internal audit report, so action 2 correctly prevents an affirmative answer under limb (b); and the limbs being separately framed, action 4 is correct. Action 3 is not, because a representation cannot take the place of the auditor's own assessment under limb (a) and cannot supply the consideration of internal audit reports which limb (b) requires. The five year tenure of the statutory auditor and the manner in which the internal audit department's fee is charged, in paragraph (6), are facts which do not bear on clause (xiv).

Which of the following sets correctly identifies the CARO 2020 clauses, from among clauses (x) to (xvi), that are engaged by the facts recorded in paragraphs (1) to (5) of the above case?
options: Clauses (xiii) and (xiv) only
Clauses (xiii), (xiv) and (xv) only
Clauses (xi), (xiii), (xiv) and (xv) only
Clauses (xiii), (xiv), (xv) and (xvi) only
questions.explanation: The eleven related party transactions and the section 177 failure in paragraphs (1) and (2) engage clause (xiii); the composition and coverage of the internal audit department and the auditor's failure to read its reports in paragraph (5) engage clause (xiv); and the transfer of a building to the managing director against shares in paragraph (3) engages clause (xv), while the cash purchase in paragraph (4) does not engage clause (xv) but remains within clause (xiii). Clause (xi) is not engaged because none of the recorded facts amounts to any fraud by or on the company, a failure of Audit Committee approval being a compliance breach and not, on these facts, fraud; and clause (xvi) is not engaged because the company is neither required to be registered under section 45-IA of the RBI Act, 1934 nor is a Core Investment Company. The set which omits clause (xv) fails to carry the building for shares transaction, which is the clearest non-cash transaction with a director in the case.

questions.question:
CASE STUDY: Amaravati Capital Markets Limited is a listed public company and a member of the Amaravati Group. Its financial year ends on 31 March 2025 and its revenue for the year was ₹14,000 crore. The following facts emerged during the audit:
(1) The company raised ₹450 crore by way of an initial public offer in June 2024 for three objects stated in the offer document. ₹20 crore of the amount earmarked for the acquisition of a data-analytics business was instead used to pay the company's salaries and rent and has not been restored; the acquisition was completed in August 2024 out of the remaining ₹40 crore. The other ₹430 crore was applied to the stated objects during the year.
(2) In September 2024 the company made a preferential allotment of equity shares raising ₹120 crore, the object stated in the notice being capital expenditure on a new campus. The auditor established that the requirements of section 42 and section 62 of the Companies Act, 2013 had been complied with, but ₹70 crore of the proceeds was used to acquire the shares of another company.
(3) In December 2024 the chief operating officer was placed under arrest for having, over the two preceding years, diverted ₹12 crore of the company's funds to entities controlled by him. The company constituted a committee of inquiry and ₹12 crore was recovered from him in February 2025. The statutory auditor did not file any report under section 143(12) of the Companies Act, 2013 in Form ADT-4 with the Central Government in respect of any matter during the year.
(4) The company has no internal audit function, the management being of the view that its processes are automated. The statutory auditor read the reports of the concurrent auditors appointed by the company's two largest lenders, and formed no view on whether the company has an internal audit system commensurate with the size and nature of its business.
(5) The company took a twenty year lease of its head office premises from a trust of which the minor children of its chairperson are the sole beneficiaries. The entire consideration for the lease was satisfied by issuing additional equity shares of the company to the trust, no cash passing either way.
(6) The company purchases software licences annually from a company in which the spouse of its whole-time director holds 60% of the paid-up equity shares. The transactions aggregated ₹35 crore during the year, the approvals required in accordance with the applicable provisions of the Companies Act were obtained, and the transactions are disclosed in the notes to the accounts as required by the applicable accounting standard.
(7) The company is registered under section 45-IA of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 as a non-banking financial company and is not a Core Investment Company (CIC). The auditor ascertained that the company has not carried on any non-banking financial or housing finance activity without a valid Certificate of Registration at any time during the year. The Amaravati Group comprises eleven companies, of which four are CICs.

Which of the following sets correctly identifies every CARO 2020 clause, from among clauses (x) to (xvi), that is engaged by the facts in the above case?
options: Clauses (x), (xi), (xiv) and (xv) only
Clauses (x), (xi), (xiii), (xiv) and (xv) only
Clauses (x), (xi), (xiii), (xiv), (xv) and (xvi) only
Clauses (x), (xi), (xii), (xiii), (xiv) and (xvi) only
questions.explanation: Clause (x) is engaged twice, by the ₹20 crore of initial public offer money applied to salaries and rent under limb (a) and by the ₹120 crore preferential allotment applied to the purchase of shares under limb (b); clause (xi) is engaged by the ₹12 crore diversion by the chief operating officer, a fraud on the company noticed and reported during the year, and by the absence of any Form ADT-4 filing; clause (xiii) is engaged by the software licences bought from the whole-time director's spouse's company; clause (xiv) is engaged by the absence of an internal audit function in a company with ₹14,000 crore of revenue; clause (xv) is engaged by the head office lease taken from the chairperson's children's trust against the issue of shares; and clause (xvi) is engaged by the registration under section 45-IA and by the four CICs in the Group. Clause (xii) alone drops out, because the company is not a Nidhi Company, and the sets which omit clause (xiii) or clause (xvi) fail to carry the related party and RBI registration facts.
